system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Taken together, the limitation package, general disclosure, buyer-knowledge bar and missing fraud carve-out would leave very little warranty protection. On top of that, the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the three biggest completion risks are unresolved:

* the Bluefen consent,
* the Riverlark payout and security discharge, and
* the AUD 420,000 bonuses missing from the funds flow.

We should reject the package as a whole and respond with our playbook positions.

---

## 1. Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

**We should not accept these.** The Seller marked its own clauses "[STANDARD]" and says they were "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". Nothing in our playbook or instructions shows any such agreement. Most of the clauses marked [STANDARD] are exactly the ones in most dispute.

* I have reviewed every clause regardless of label.
* **Recommendation:** Our cover note should say expressly that Wattlebridge has not agreed any clause, the disclosure framework or the limitation package, and that all positions remain open until a signed SPA. This stops the Seller later arguing that we accepted the package through our conduct in negotiations.

---

## 2. Limitation package

### 2.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m
* **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback. It can be used **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft, and none has been given.
* **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. We cannot concede 20% at this stage.
* **Internal note:** The Seller's opening cap (20%) and claims period (18 months) exactly match our two authority-gated fallbacks. This may be coincidence or market convention. It is still worth checking internally that our fallback positions have not been shared outside the deal team.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Mechanism | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar once exceeded (tipping) |

* The Seller's basket is five times ours and works as a deductible, so we would absorb the first AUD 250,000 permanently.
* A AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude many real claims, for example individual supplier or employee items.
* **Push back:** Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months plus a "catch-all" limitation
* **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
* **Hidden override:** The proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is the most dangerous drafting point in the package. By default it would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general regime. That conflicts with our principle of keeping categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.
* **Push back:** Insist on 24 months. Reverse the default so that limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Each other category should have its own stated regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
* The Seller proposes the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". For a share sale, this would cap our recovery for not actually getting the shares at 20% of the price.
* **Push back:** Require a separate regime:
  * cap at 100% of the price,
  * a claims period of at least six years,
  * outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
* There is **no fraud carve-out**. As drafted, caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would arguably protect the Seller even for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.
* Courts may decline to enforce some of these exclusions against fraud anyway. We should not rely on that.
* **Push back (non-negotiable):** Expressly carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is not something the deal team or anyone else can waive.

---

## 3. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter)

### 3.1 General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2)
* The Seller seeks to disclose against the warranties:
  * the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and everything "referred to" in it),
  * the Accounts,
  * the statutory registers, and
  * all "publicly searchable corporate records".
* The effect is that any fact anywhere in that material defeats a warranty claim, whether or not it was fairly identified.
* **Push back:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should count only if it is **specific and fair**, meaning it identifies the matter with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to assess its nature and scope. There should be no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.

### 3.2 Non-admission (DL 1.4)
* A non-admission clause is broadly acceptable.
* We should make sure the SPA states that DL 1.4 does not qualify any condition, covenant, indemnity or completion deliverable. Otherwise the Seller could rely on it to argue that the Bluefen consent or the Riverlark discharge is "not legally required".

### 3.3 Why the specific disclosures matter
The specific disclosures (DL 2–10) are actually helpful. They confirm the gaps in the Seller's position. However, combined with the buyer-knowledge bar (section 4 below), they would be used to stop us claiming on exactly those issues. For that reason, these risks must be dealt with through **conditions, completion deliverables and specific indemnities**, not warranties.

---

## 4. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

* The proposed bar excludes any claim about a matter known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". Together with general disclosure, this would largely neutralise the warranties.
* **Push back:** Delete the clause.
* If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should:
  * refer to **Seller** knowledge, limited to named individuals, after reasonable enquiry;
  * never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 5. Completion risks (confirmed open by the Disclosure Letter)

### 5.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002; DL 2)
* Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). DL 2 confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
* The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once a written consent is delivered. That is insufficient for a customer of this importance. A consent that is conditional, or whose conditions are unmet, may not be effective at all.
* **Push back:** Make it a condition precedent to Completion that:
  * an effective written consent under cl 11.2 is obtained, and
  * the Seller provides evidence that every cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.

  Only the Buyer should be able to waive this condition. Strengthen the endeavours obligation, and include a Buyer termination right if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

### 5.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003; DL 3)
* About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. The Seller offers a release "following Completion", which would leave us owning a company whose assets may still be secured to Riverlark.
* **Push back:** Require the following as completion deliverables:
  * a current payout letter (including interest, fees and break costs, not an "approximate" figure);
  * repayment **directly from Completion funds** to Riverlark;
  * executed security releases, PPSR discharges and the return of any title documents, effective at Completion.
* A post-completion release is acceptable only if both:
  * Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release, and
  * Amelia Frost approves in writing.

### 5.3 Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005; DL 5)
* The AUD 420,000 in conditional completion bonuses has been deliberately left out of the funds flow as "a matter for the Seller". However:
  * the bonuses appear to be Company obligations triggered by Completion, so economically we would bear them; and
  * DL 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
* **Push back:** Do one of the following:
  * add a specific funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (treated as Debt or transaction costs) and paying them through payroll; or
  * require the Seller to fund them, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.

  The funds flow must not exclude them silently.

---

## 6. Other specific issues

### 6.1 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL 4)
* The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. The real risk is wider: we may not own or be free to use the SOW3 Project Materials, and third parties could bring claims.
* DL 4 itself says there is no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
* The AUD 180,000 open amount is **not independently verified in either direction**. We should not treat it as owed, or as paid.
* **Push back:**
  * Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of title to, or transfer of, the Project Materials, related infringement claims, and Ironquay claims.
  * Keep the SOW3 cure: once cleared payment of every SOW3 fee is evidenced, and ideally a confirmatory assignment is obtained, the transfer under cl 7.3 occurs.
  * Request bank-level evidence of the payment status.

### 6.2 Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL 6)
* The Seller says the incident is "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter, however, says access, scope and any notification requirement are all undetermined.
* We should accept neither conclusion. There is **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction**, so we should not put a dollar demand on it.
* **Push back:** Require:
  * preservation of all logs and evidence;
  * a completed investigation, including an assessment of whether notification is required under applicable privacy law;
  * regular updates to the Buyer before Completion, with access to the findings;
  * consultation with us before any notification or regulator contact.

  We should keep open the option of a specific indemnity or warranty once the facts are known.

### 6.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL 8)
* The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. Its own disclosure says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three related AUD 110,000 renewals should be read together.
* **Action:** Assess them. Request the contracts and confirm:
  * timing against the signing date and the conduct-of-business covenants,
  * termination rights,
  * accrual treatment, and
  * whether they were properly approved.
* We should **not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Any adjustment should depend on what the assessment shows.

### 6.4 Tax and IP warranties
* The Seller describes these as "settled under the general regime". They are **not** settled. They remain open, separate categories.
* Reject any wording that folds them into the general cap or time limits. We should not assume unlimited liability, and we should not treat the point as resolved.

### 6.5 Title (DD-012; DL 10)
* The DD-012 share register is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof, and DL 10 concedes we have not verified it.
* **Push back:** Require independent evidence, including:
  * our own ASIC and PPSR searches;
  * original share certificates;
  * a warranty that the shares are free of encumbrances, options and pre-emption rights, plus any necessary waivers;
  * board and shareholder resolutions and evidence of Seller authority and capacity;
  * a Title warranty under the separate fundamental regime in section 2.4.

### 6.6 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
* These are not playbook items, and the Disclosure Letter does not say that consent is required for either.
* **Action:**
  * Have our lawyers confirm the reading of each provision.
  * Make the lease notification a completion deliverable or covenant.
  * Confirm that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale.

---

## 7. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [STANDARD] labels / efficiency note | Claims mutual clearance | Reject in writing; nothing is agreed |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) |
| 3 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping** |
| 4 | Claims period | 18 months + catch-all override | **24 months**; delete the override; separate regimes |
| 5 | Title / fundamental | Same as general | **100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket and knowledge bar** |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Full carve-out from all limits** (non-waivable) |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers / discoverable | **Delete**; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons, reasonable enquiry, with carve-outs |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item AUD 420k + on-costs, or Seller-funded with indemnity** |
| 12 | Ironquay | SOW3-payment-only indemnity | **Broaden, keep SOW3 cure, verify payment** |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, updates**; no assumed breach or demand |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess**; no automatic Debt or deduction |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Open; separate categories** |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent searches, certificates, authority evidence** |

**Internal actions**
* **Fallback authority:** We have no authority to concede the 20% cap or the 18-month period. If the team wants either in reserve, we need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).
* **Riverlark approval:** Any post-completion Riverlark arrangement also needs her approval.
* **Confidentiality check:** Consider the check on fallback confidentiality noted in section 2.1.

I can prepare the cover note and an issues-list mark-up on this basis if helpful.
=== END ADVICE ===
